title: embed.js cached at CDN edges for up to a year with no invalidation step -- deploys don't propagate
description:
Discovered chasing an apparently-inconsistent deploy while integrating and then
iterating on Pilobol.us's Auritus embed (2026-09-14/15). Across several
consecutive fixes and deploys to aurit.us/embed.js this session, different
requests -- sometimes even from the same browser tab, sometimes a fresh tab
-- returned DIFFERENT versions of the file, days-to-minutes apart in what
they contained. Root cause:

curl -sI https://aurit.us/embed.js
  cache-control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=31536000
  x-cache: Hit from cloudfront
  x-amz-cf-pop: MIA50-P7
  age: 329

s-maxage=31536000 is ONE YEAR. This is Amplify Hosting's own default
behavior for static assets served from a Next.js app's public/ directory --
nothing in this repo's CDK/Amplify config sets it explicitly (checked; no
Cache-Control override anywhere for site/public/embed.js). Once any given
CloudFront edge/POP has cached a response, it will keep serving that exact
byte-for-byte snapshot to every request that lands on it for up to a year,
regardless of how many times the origin is redeployed -- there is no build
step or deploy hook in this repo that issues a CloudFront invalidation.
Different edges around the world end up permanently (well, for up to a
year) stuck at whatever snapshot they individually had cached at their own
last cache-miss, which can be from any point in the deploy history.

This means: every deploy of embed.js is, in practice, only reliably visible
to *new* edges that haven't cached anything yet. Any edge already primed
before your change goes out keeps serving the old file indefinitely. For a
component that literally IS the product being distributed to every
integrating site, that's serious -- it means bug fixes and feature
ships to the embed don't actually reach existing readers/sites reliably,
with no error, no warning, and no way for an integrator to tell they're
running a stale copy short of diffing the file's contents by hand (which is
how this was found).

Two independent fixes, either meaningfully improves this, ideally both:

1. Version the filename with a content hash (e.g. embed.abc123.js) and have
   the published snippet's default src point at that, OR keep embed.js as a
   stable alias that's explicitly configured with a SHORT s-maxage (seconds
   to low minutes, not a year) so ordinary CDN cache expiry does the right
   thing without any deploy-time action needed.
2. Add a CloudFront invalidation step to the site's deploy pipeline (a
   simple `aws cloudfront create-invalidation --paths /embed.js` after
   the Amplify build completes) so existing edges pick up new bytes
   immediately on every deploy, regardless of the cache-control policy.

Filed at P1 because this isn't cosmetic -- it means recent fixes (including
some from this same session: the data-auritus-api default, the auto-boot
currentScript bug, the native-controls swap, the automatic pause markers)
may currently be invisible to some fraction of real traffic depending on
which CloudFront edge they land on, with no way to know from the outside.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Fixed: added site/customHttp.yml setting Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=60, must-revalidate specifically for /embed.js. Amplify Hosting auto-detects this file at the app root with no other config needed. This is fix option 1 from the original description (short s-maxage instead of the inherited one-year default) -- didn't do the content-hashed-filename version, since that would also require updating every published embed snippet's src (this site's own examples, every integrator's copied snippet) to point at the new filename, a bigger and more disruptive change. A CloudFront edge will now pick up a new deploy within a minute, not up to a year.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Correction: site/customHttp.yml never actually took effect -- confirmed live through a full successful deploy (job 109) with the app's customHeaders field (aws amplify get-app) still empty and aurit.us/embed.js still serving s-maxage=31536000. The real mechanism for this app is the Amplify App resource's own customHeaders field, set directly:

aws amplify update-app --app-id d1xec2o22j5yq2 --custom-headers file:///path/to/headers.yml

(or equivalently via Console -> App settings -> Hosting -> Custom headers). Confirmed: took effect on the very next request, no redeploy needed. Removed the inert file from the repo so it doesn't point the next person at a mechanism that does nothing on this app. Current live value: cache-control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=60, must-revalidate.
